title: On the stability of learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.35856v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Learning algorithms are usually analyzed under the assumption that informative gradients are continuously available. But this is not always true---learning signals in biological neural networks, for example, may be sparse, local, and only intermittently available at any given synapse. In this work, we show that if gradient information is noisy and only intermittently available, learning may be unstable. In particular, even if average learning dynamics converge to the correct optimum, variance in learning may be asymptotically infinite. We explore this point in a number of analytically tractable settings, including single-layer and multi-layer linear networks, and derive explicit conditions under which learning is stable. These conditions complement, but are conceptually distinct from, existing conditions related to the stability of stochastic gradient descent. translated_abstract: 学习算法通常是在“信息性梯度持续可用”的假设下进行分析的。但事实并非总是如此——例如，生物神经网络中的学习信号可能是稀疏的、局部的，并且在任意给定突触处仅间歇性地可用。在这项工作中，我们证明：如果梯度信息是带噪声的且仅间歇性可用，学习可能会变得不稳定。特别地，即使平均学习动态收敛到正确的最优值，学习的方差也可能渐近地趋于无穷大。我们在若干可解析求解的设置中探讨了这一问题，包括单层和多层线性网络，并推导出了学习保持稳定的显式条件。这些条件与现有的关于随机梯度下降稳定性的条件互为补充，但在概念上与之截然不同。我们的工作表明，无偏的信用分配并不足以实现可靠的学习。
tldr: 该研究证明当梯度信息带噪且仅间歇性可用时，即使平均学习动态收敛到最优解，学习的方差也可能渐近发散，并在线性网络中推导出了学习稳定的显式条件。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that learning can be unstable when gradient information is noisy and only intermittently available—even if the average learning dynamics converge, the variance may diverge asymptotically—and derives explicit stability conditions for single- and multi-layer linear networks.
